title: Enterprise Go‑Live Readiness & Escalation Guide
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines the combined go‑live readiness checklist and escalation pathways for enterprise customers adopting Redwood Inference (hosted, Dedicated, or Private). It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, SRE, and Onboarding Engineers. Use this guide to: prepare the account for production traffic, perform last‑mile validation, and execute a fast, structured escalation when issues threaten customer SLAs.

Scope:
- Applies to enterprise onboarding windows, major feature launches (e.g., model rollouts, routing policy changes), and first 30 days of production traffic.
- Covers technical validation, operational handoff, and 3‑tier escalation procedures.

Quick summary (one line):
- Goal: deterministic, auditable go‑live and rapid mitigation for production incidents with clear owner handoffs and communication templates.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): overall customer relationship, schedules go‑live window, owns QBR inputs.
- Onboarding Engineer: runs integration tests, signs off prelaunch checklist.
- Support Engineer: first responder for production issues (Triage tier).
- SRE / Infra Owner: handles platform incidents that affect multiple customers (Escalation tier).
- Account Executive (AE): commercial contact for contractual questions.

Pre‑Go‑Live readiness checklist (must be completed and signed by Onboarding Engineer and CSM):
1) Account & Access
   - Verify API key provisioning and RBAC roles for customer engineers (Admin, Service, Readonly).
   - Confirm network allowlists, VPC peering, or private endpoint configuration for Private deployments.
2) Capacity & Routing
   - Confirm Dedicated pool reservation or confirm hosted tier quotas sufficient for expected TPS and bursts.
   - Confirm routing policy (primary model, fallback model list) and regional failovers.
3) Performance validation (acceptance criteria):
   - P50 latency <= 80ms, P95 latency <= 200ms for baseline generation workload (1k token avg).
   - Error rate (5xx+4xx) < 0.5% over 10k requests.
   - Token cost within agreed budget +/-15% during a 1‑hour stress window.
4) Functional validation
   - Run end‑to‑end integration test suite (see Test matrix below).
   - Confirm streaming and tool‑calling flows if used.
5) Observability and alerts
   - Dashboard access granted to customer (Console) and to CSM/SE.
   - Alerts configured: API error rate > 0.5% over 5m, P95 latency > 350ms (hosted), KV cache eviction rate > 1% per minute.
6) Rollback & Fallback plan
   - Document automatic fallback models and traffic shifting policy (canary %, time window).
   - Pre‑define manual rollback steps and contact list.

Acceptance signoff: Onboarding Engineer: ____________________  Date: ______  CSM: ____________________  Date: ______

Test matrix (example commands):
- Connectivity test (cURL):
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-small-2025","input":"Smoke test: hello world"}'

- Streaming smoke test (SDK snippet):
  node ./tests/streaming-smoke.js --key=$API_KEY --model=redwood-small-2025

- KV cache verification (probe):
  1) Send repeated prefixes to warm cache; 2) measure tokens saved vs baseline; expect cache hit ratio > 40% for typical chat workloads.

Operational runbook: immediate triage (Support Engineer)
1) Triage (0–10 minutes):
   - Confirm customer and service impact: Are requests failing (5xx) or timing out? Is degradation limited to a route/model/region?
   - Gather: request_id, model name, region, client IP, timestamp range, sample request/response.
   - Check dashboards: error rate, latency P95, active connections, KV cache eviction rate.
   - If reproducible, collect a minimal repro and test in a staging account (do not escalate credentials).
2) Mitigation (10–30 minutes):
   - Apply temporary traffic steering: switch to fallback model or route to Dedicated pool.
   - If Private deployment networking issue, recommend customer perform NAT gateway check and DNS resolution (see Known Issues).
   - Open internal support ticket and tag severity (see Severity definitions).
3) Escalate to SRE/Engineering (30+ minutes if unresolved OR immediately for Sev1):
   - Provide incident summary, timestamps, customer impact, and mitigation steps taken.
   - Attach logs, heap/metrics links, and any reproducer.

Severity definitions and response targets:
- Sev1 (Customer outage / production feature block): "Production unavailable or > 50% of traffic affected" -> Target: Acknowledge < 15m, Mitigation plan < 30m, Next update every 15m.
- Sev2 (Degraded but functional): "Performance > 3x expected P95 or error rate > 1%" -> Acknowledge < 30m, Mitigation plan < 2 hours, Updates every 60m.
- Sev3 (Minor/feature degradation): "Reduced quality or edge case errors" -> Acknowledge < 4 hours, Mitigation plan in next business day.

Escalation contacts & channels:
- Slack (primary): #support-enterprise (alerting integration posts incident card), @oncall‑sre for Sev1.
- PagerDuty: SRE-oncall schedule (link in internal ops).
- Email escalation: enterprise-incidents@redwood.ai (use for external updates to customer execs if directed by CSM).
- Phone: SRE escalation phone list (CSMs have access in PagerDuty notes).

Communication templates (use for external customer updates):
- Initial acknowledgement (to customer):
  Subject: Redwood Incident — [Short summary] — {Incident ID}
  Body: Thank you for reporting. We have identified an issue affecting {feature}. Impact: {describe}. Mitigation: {actions taken}. Next update: {time}. Owner: {CSM name} / {Support engineer}.

- Post‑incident summary: include timeline, root cause (if known), corrective actions, and rollback changes.

Known Issues & Workarounds (current as of 2026‑02‑20):
1) KV cache eviction spike after large prefix churn (hosted + dedicated)
   - Symptom: sudden drop in cache hit ratio and higher token usage/cost.
   - Probable cause: sustained many unique prefixes exceeding cache memory slab allocations.
   - Short‑term workaround: reduce prefix variance on client; apply per‑customer cache size override (SE must request to eng‑runtime).
   - Long‑term: runtime will add per‑tenant adaptive cache eviction (roadmap Q2 2026).
2) Private deployment DNS timeouts on new VPCs
   - Symptom: Intermittent 504s during lookup, customers behind strict firewall/NAT.
   - Workaround: Ensure resolvers list includes company internal DNS; enable DNS caching on edge; confirm outbound TCP/UDP to Redwood control plane endpoints on allowed ports.
3) Model fallback incompatibility for custom finetuned artifacts
   - Symptom: Fallback model returns structurally different JSON payloads causing client parsing errors.
   - Workaround: Map schema transformations at the routing layer (SE creates a translation shim) or pin to compatible fallback models.

Observability checks to run during initial 72 hours post‑go‑live:
- Daily for first 3 days: check dashboard P95 latency, error rate, token cost, model fallback frequency, KV cache hit ratio.
- Weekly: regression test on canonical prompt set; compare embedding similarity drift.

QBR & health packet template (metrics to include):
- Activation: % of seats / tokens used vs committed (monthly)
- Performance: P95 latency, error rate, average token throughput (rps & tokens/s)
- Reliability: uptime (30d), number of Sev1/Sev2 incidents, MTTR per incident
- Cost efficiency: effective $ / 1M tokens (hosted) or GPU utilization (Dedicated)
- Product quality: top 5 failing prompts and suggested mitigation (prompt fixes, model switch)

Example QBR slide outline (bullets):
1) Executive summary: usage highlights and commercial notes
2) Key metrics (activation, latency, errors) with 30/90/180 day trend charts
3) Incidents since last QBR: root cause and corrective actions
4) Optimization opportunities: batching, quantization suggestion, fallback tuning
5) Roadmap items affecting the customer (e.g., private control plane improvements)

Post‑incident follow‑ups and handback to CSM:
- After incident closure, SRE provides a short remediation log and owner for long‑term fixes.
- CSM schedules a debrief with customer within 5 business days to cover impact and mitigation.
- If remediation requires configuration change, SE creates a change request and documents rollback steps.

Change management for production configs (not exhaustive):
- All config changes affecting customer routing or quotas require: a) Change ticket (JIRA) b) CSM notification c) Canaries (10% traffic max) d) 24h monitoring window.

Appendix A — Example minimal reproducer (sanitized):
- Request payload that triggers a 5xx: {
  "model": "redwood-large-2025",
  "input": "<long conversation with > 16k tokens>"
}
- Recommended mitigation: trim history to last 8k tokens and route to a long‑context variant.

Appendix B — Escalation checklist (one‑page):
- Incident created and severity set: Y/N
- Reproducer captured: Y/N
- Mitigation in place (fallback/route): Y/N
- SRE paged (for Sev1/2): Y/N
- Customer executive update scheduled: Y/N
